terra.problem: Saying Job isn't asking anything for himself excludes him from a question about mortals. The text doesn't make that exclusion.
Calling God the audience Job is worried about adds an unmarked feeling and confuses whom Job is speaking about with his audience.
Saying the person could not answer on any try after the first goes beyond Job's statement of not answering once in a thousand.
The passage doesn't say that every action in the list is something only God could do.
Rahab could be confused with the better-known Rahab of Jericho. The explanation needs to distinguish them.
The explanation repeats that Job can't catch his breath without adding much. It reads flat and generic.
Calling the smile fake adds something Job doesn't say. He imagines changing his expression and smiling.
Job says that after he washes, God would plunge him into the pit. Saying the scrubbing doesn't get him clean blurs that sequence.
Job says there is no mediator. The text doesn't say he is looking for one.
The explanation repeats that good deeds aren't mentioned and gives little beyond the answer. It reads flat and generic.
Job says there is no deliverance from God's hand. Calling that his fear adds an unmarked feeling.
The stamper comparison doesn't follow: being a stamper doesn't establish that Papa knows what it's like to be pressed into shape.
Saying Job doesn't use stone because it doesn't mold invents his reason for choosing the comparison.
Job says he cannot lift his head even if righteous. The explanation extends that statement to the guilty case, where Job says woe to him.
The explanation says there is no light in Job's description, but Job says even the light is like darkness.
